page.layout: One column of running text with a centred-left section heading "4. GENVS CAVSSAE." in capitals partway down. No marginal notes. Running head at top with page number at top right. Catchword and signature at the foot.

main_text.p: niam improbus erat Manasses, subticue-runt eius nomen. Huius libri auctorem secutus Leonhardus Crentzemius, uir multae lectionis, & edita Chronologia bene de Ecclesia meritus, statuit Habacu cum docuisse circa annum ab Orbe condito 3272. ante Christum natum an. 699.
Istud extra controuersiam est, docui-sse Prophetam ante excidium urbis Hie-rosolymorum & Babylonicam captiuitatem: cum diuinitus edoctus praenuncia-uerit Chaldaeorum expeditionem in Iu-daeam.
main_text.head: 4. GENVS CAVSSAE.
main_text.p: Nihil dubium est, totam hanc Prophetiam referendam nobis esse ad iudiciale genus causae. Etenim qualitem de Prouidentia erga genus humanum, praecipue uero erga Ecclesiam, etiam Pij (cum eos aduersa premunt, & successus improborum male habent) Deo moueat: & quomodo is prouidentiam, iusticiam & misericordiam suam, aduersus sinistra hominum iudicia, tueatur & demonstret, euidenter ostendit. Facit autem eo, ut discamus non sapere supra quam oportet, sed ad sobrietatem, Rom.12.3. & ut Dei po-

page.notes: Printed text was not affected by any damage. Left edge of the first line is cut off, so the opening word is a fragment ("niam"). The catchword "tius" and the foot mark "4" are read from the bottom of the scan. The hyphen in "subticue-runt" and "docui-sse" is a printed line-end hyphen. Long s has been written as plain s throughout. The word "successus" and "sinistra" were read clearly and are not marked.
